framing.summary: The pyramid is a starting guess, not a verdict. OCEBM 2011 lets you move a study down for poor quality, imprecision, indirectness or inconsistency, and up for a very large effect. GRADE does the same per outcome: RCT evidence starts high, observational evidence starts low, and five domains move it down (risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias) while three can move observational evidence up (large effect, dose-response, plausible confounding that would shrink the effect).

sources.title: Explanation of the 2011 OCEBM Levels of Evidence
Cochrane Handbook v6.5 (2024), ch. 14 on GRADE

framing.potency_scale: 1-10 strength of evidence for a causal treatment effect when the study is done well. 'range' shows how far real studies swing either side.
framing.effectiveness_scale: 1-10 how practical the design is for a full-rota LED to finish and publish.

levels.label: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
levels.short: Pooled, appraised evidence from all relevant randomised trials.
levels.ocebm_2011: Level 1 for treatment benefit and harm.
levels.grade_start: Inherits the certainty of the included RCTs (starts high).

potency.explanation: Top of the pile only when the trials underneath are good. Pooling small, biased trials just gives a precise wrong answer.
raises: Consistent effects (low tau, narrow prediction interval)
Pre-registered protocol (PROSPERO) and full search incl. Embase/CENTRAL
GRADE Summary of Findings with high/moderate certainty
lowers: High risk of bias in included trials (no allocation concealment, unblinded subjective outcomes)
Indirectness (different population, implant or comparator) - the commonest downgrade in fracture surgery
Redundancy: the 6th MA on the same question adds nothing

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: High. No patients, no ethics, works on evenings and weekends.
effectiveness_for_him.time: Mean 67 weeks registration to publication (Borah 2017). Realistic 10-18 months for you with a team of 3-5.
effectiveness_for_him.team: You + 1 independent second reviewer + arbiter + librarian + statistician (for MA) + consultant senior author.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: None. Register on PROSPERO before screening.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF. Your best first-author engine.

examples_ortho.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty Versus Hemiarthroplasty for Displaced Femoral Neck Fracture: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Pairwise MA of RCTs in a top journal, updated after a big new trial (HEALTH). Shows the 'new RCT since last MA' justification.

examples_ortho.title: Interventions for treating proximal humeral fractures in adults
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Cochrane review with GRADE Summary of Findings tables. The template for rigour.

examples_ortho.title: Operative management of displaced fractures of the distal radius is associated with improved function but not in older adults: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Recent SR/MA of RCTs in a UK journal on a topic close to your distal radius audit. Shows how an age subgroup drives the message.

typical_numbers.fact: Mean 67.3 weeks from PROSPERO registration to publication; mean team of 5; median 63 full texts screened; about 3% of retrieved records end up included.
typical_numbers.source: Borah R, Brown AW, Capers PL, Kaiser KA. Analysis of the time and workers needed to conduct systematic reviews of medical interventions using data from the PROSPERO registry. BMJ Open. 2017;7(2):e012545.

typical_numbers.fact: About 682 SRs were indexed in MEDLINE in a single month in 2014, roughly triple the 2004 rate. Many are redundant.
typical_numbers.source: Page MJ, Shamseer L, Altman DG, Tetzlaff J, Sampson M, Tricco AC, et al. Epidemiology and reporting characteristics of systematic reviews of biomedical research: a cross-sectional study. PLoS Med. 2016;13(5):e1002028.

typical_numbers.fact: Orthopaedic intervention SRs usually screen 1,000-5,000 records and include 5-30 studies; pairwise RCT MAs often pool 5-15 trials with a few hundred to a few thousand patients.
typical_numbers.source: Rule of thumb from the KB and the yield rate in Borah 2017. Not a single meta-research figure.

levels.label: Randomised controlled trial
levels.short: Chance decides who gets what, so groups differ only by treatment.
levels.ocebm_2011: Level 2 (an individual RCT) for treatment benefit; Level 1 only as part of an SR.
levels.grade_start: Starts high; downgrade for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias.

subtypes.name: Double/triple-blind or sham-controlled
subtypes.note: Strongest against expectation bias. Possible in surgery with sham arms (FIDELITY, CSAW), or blinded outcome assessors.

subtypes.name: Open (unblinded) with blinded assessor
subtypes.note: Normal in surgery. Fine for hard outcomes (revision, death); weaker for PROMs and pain.

subtypes.name: Individual vs cluster
subtypes.note: Cluster trials randomise wards or hospitals (CRISTAL). Need more patients because of the intracluster correlation; analyse at the right level.

subtypes.name: Explanatory vs pragmatic
subtypes.note: Pragmatic trials (DRAFFT, AIM, PROFHER) test treatments in normal NHS conditions. Better generalisability, more noise. Use PRECIS-2 to place your design.

subtypes.name: Superiority / non-inferiority / equivalence
subtypes.note: Non-inferiority needs a justified margin and a per-protocol sensitivity analysis (AIM).

potency.explanation: Randomisation deals with confounders you know and the ones you do not. Quality still varies a lot.
raises: Adequate power and low loss to follow-up
lowers: Small sample (median Fragility Index of 2 in sports-surgery RCTs)

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Low as chief investigator; high as site PI, Associate PI or collaborator on portfolio trials.
effectiveness_for_him.time: 3-6 years from idea to result for a full trial. Your fast route is joining existing NIHR trials (FACT.1).
effectiveness_for_him.team: CTU, trial statistician, trial manager, funded research staff, many sites.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: Sponsor + HRA + REC (+ MHRA for drugs/devices). Registration before first patient.
effectiveness_for_him.typical_months_to_publication: 36-72 (as lead); collaborator papers arrive with the trial

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF. Collaborator listing under a group name alone is excluded. Associate PI scores separately (once).

examples_ortho.title: Percutaneous fixation with Kirschner wires versus volar locking plate fixation in adults with dorsally displaced fracture of distal radius: randomised controlled trial
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: UK pragmatic multicentre RCT (DRAFFT). Surgeon-delivered interventions, so no blinding of surgeon or patient; outcome is a PROM (PRWE).
examples_ortho.verification: PMID-title match on PubMed + journal/year confirmed via Europe PMC REST API (2026-10-21)

examples_ortho.title: Arthroscopic subacromial decompression for subacromial shoulder pain (CSAW): a multicentre, pragmatic, parallel group, placebo-controlled, three-group, randomised surgical trial
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: UK three-arm trial with a placebo (arthroscopy only) arm and a no-treatment arm. A model of how to design out expectation bias.

examples_ortho.title: Effect of Aspirin vs Enoxaparin on Symptomatic Venous Thromboembolism in Patients Undergoing Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: The CRISTAL Randomized Trial
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Registry-nested cluster-randomised crossover trial: hospitals, not patients, were randomised. Relevant to your VTE prophylaxis interest.

examples_ortho.title: Arthroscopic partial meniscectomy versus sham surgery for a degenerative meniscal tear
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Sham-controlled, patient- and assessor-blinded surgical RCT (FIDELITY). Shows that blinding in surgery is possible and changes conclusions.

examples_ortho.title: Close Contact Casting vs Surgery for Initial Treatment of Unstable Ankle Fractures in Older Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: UK pragmatic non-inferiority RCT (AIM). Good example of a non-inferiority margin set on a PROM (Olerud-Molander).

typical_numbers.fact: Median Fragility Index of 2 among statistically significant sports-surgery RCTs.
typical_numbers.source: Khan M, Evaniew N, Gichuru M, et al. The fragility of statistically significant findings from randomized trials in sports surgery. Am J Sports Med. 2017.

typical_numbers.fact: Median of 30 patients per group across 66 sports-surgery RCTs.
typical_numbers.source: Secondary analysis of the Khan dataset, PMC6536113 (PeerJ 2019)

typical_numbers.fact: UK NIHR-funded trauma trials usually recruit 250-1,500 patients across 20-50 NHS sites (DRAFFT 461, PROFHER 250, AIM 620).
typical_numbers.source: Sample sizes from the trial papers listed in examples_ortho (approximate).

levels.label: Non-randomised controlled / quasi-experimental
levels.short: Compared groups, but allocation not random (before-after, time series).
levels.grade_start: Starts low (or high if assessed with ROBINS-I, then downgraded).

subtypes.name: Controlled before-and-after
subtypes.note: Intervention site vs a control site, measured before and after.

subtypes.name: Interrupted time series
subtypes.note: Many data points before and after a change (Neuburger 2015 on the NHFD). Strongest quasi-design.

subtypes.name: Historical control
subtypes.note: New technique vs previous cohort. Weak: everything else changed too.

potency.explanation: Useful when randomising is unethical or impossible (national policy, pathway changes). Confounding by time and selection is the main threat.
raises: A control group or control outcome
Large effect that appears exactly at the change
lowers: Regression to the mean (started after a bad month)

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Moderate. Pathway changes at Blackpool can be evaluated this way.
effectiveness_for_him.team: You, supervisor, data analyst or statistician.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: Often research (HRA tool); may be framed as service evaluation if purely local.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF.

examples_ortho.title: The impact of a national clinician-led audit initiative on care and mortality after hip fracture in England: an external evaluation using time trends in non-audit data
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Quasi-experimental (interrupted time-series style) evaluation of the NHFD and Best Practice Tariff using HES data. No randomisation possible, so trends do the work.

typical_numbers.fact: Segmented regression needs at least 3 data points per segment, and ideally 8-12 before and after, to estimate level and slope change.
typical_numbers.source: Standard ITS guidance (Cochrane EPOC); rule of thumb.

levels.reporting_guideline: TREND (non-randomised evaluations) or STROBE; SQUIRE 2.0 if framed as QI

levels.label: Prospective cohort study
levels.short: Recruit now, measure exposure, follow forward for outcomes.
levels.ocebm_2011: Level 2-3 for prognosis (inception cohort is Level 2); Level 3 for treatment.
levels.grade_start: Starts low; can be upgraded for large effect or dose-response.

potency.explanation: Data are collected on purpose, with definitions fixed in advance. Still exposed to confounding.
raises: Inception cohort (everyone recruited at the same clinical point)

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Moderate. Needs consent, REC approval and someone to collect follow-up.
effectiveness_for_him.team: You, supervisor, research nurse or data collectors, statistician.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF.

examples_ortho.title: Early mortality after hip fracture: is delay before surgery important?
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Prospective single-centre cohort from Nottingham. Classic example of a large prospectively collected local database.

examples_ortho.title: Effect of comorbidities and postoperative complications on mortality after hip fracture in elderly people: prospective observational cohort study
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Same Nottingham database, a different question, a different paper. Shows how a good prospective database feeds several papers.

typical_numbers.fact: Need roughly 10-20 outcome events per predictor in a regression model; a 5% complication rate with 8 predictors needs about 1,600-3,200 patients.
typical_numbers.source: Events-per-variable rule (KB Part A FINER section).

levels.label: Retrospective cohort study (incl. registry)
levels.short: Look back through existing records, follow exposure to outcome.
levels.ocebm_2011: Level 3 for treatment; Level 2-3 for prognosis if complete.

potency.explanation: Cheap and fast. Only as good as the records. Large national registries sit at the top of this range.
raises: Clear exposure definition and index date
lowers: Selection to treatment by surgeon preference (confounding by indication)
Outcome missed because patients went elsewhere

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: High for single-site Blackpool data; slower for registries.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: Usually research: sponsor + HRA (often no REC if anonymised to the team). Ask R&D about a local route.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF.

examples_ortho.title: Association Between Wait Time and 30-Day Mortality in Adults Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Population-based retrospective cohort from routinely collected Ontario data. Uses a clinically meaningful threshold and matching.

examples_ortho.title: Waiting time for hip fracture surgery: hospital variation, causes, and effects on postoperative mortality: data on 37,708 operations reported to the Norwegian Hip fracture Register from 2014 to 2018
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: National registry analysis published in a UK journal. Registry design with hospital variation as an extra angle.

typical_numbers.fact: Population or registry cohorts often exceed 10,000 patients (Pincus about 42,000; Norwegian Hip Fracture Register 37,708 operations). Single-centre retrospective cohorts in BJO/Injury typically report 100-1,000 patients.
typical_numbers.source: Example papers; the single-centre range is a rule of thumb.

levels.reporting_guideline: STROBE + RECORD (routinely collected data); TARGET if emulating a trial

levels.label: Case-control study
levels.short: Start with the outcome, look back for exposures.
levels.ocebm_2011: Level 4 for treatment; Level 3-4 for harms.

potency.explanation: The right tool for rare outcomes (PJI, tendon rupture). Recall and selection bias are the risks. Gives odds ratios, not risks.
raises: Nested in a defined cohort or database
Controls from the same source population
Exposure measured from records, not memory
lowers: Hospital controls who differ from cases

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: High for rare complications at Blackpool (e.g. risk factors for deep infection).
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: Research (HRA tool); sponsor + HRA, REC depends on identifiability.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF.

examples_ortho.title: Risk factors for prosthetic joint infection: case-control study
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Matched case-control study for a rare outcome (PJI). The textbook reason to choose case-control.

examples_ortho.title: Increased risk of achilles tendon rupture with quinolone antibacterial use, especially in elderly patients taking oral corticosteroids
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Nested case-control in a large GP database. Shows interaction (age x steroids) analysed properly.

typical_numbers.fact: 1-4 controls per case; gains in power flatten after 4 controls per case.
typical_numbers.source: Standard epidemiology teaching.

levels.appraisal_tool: ROBINS-E; Newcastle-Ottawa (common in ortho but weak)

levels.label: Cross-sectional study / survey
levels.short: A snapshot: prevalence or practice at one point in time.
levels.ocebm_2011: Level 2-4 depending on question (local current survey is Level 1 for 'how common is it here?').
levels.grade_start: Starts low for effects; fine for prevalence and practice variation.

potency.explanation: Good for 'what do surgeons do?' and 'how common is it?'. Cannot show cause. Response rate decides credibility.
lowers: Low response (median physician web response about 35%)

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: High. Staff surveys are quick; national reach via BOTA/BOA and societies.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: HRA tool first. Staff-only surveys: often HRA approval without REC, or university ethics. Patient surveys: usually REC.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF. Pick the journal with care; many editors desk-reject low-response surveys.

examples_ortho.title: Variation of Practice in Prophylactic Protocol to Reduce Prosthetic Joint Infection in Primary Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A National Survey in the United Kingdom
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: UK national practice-variation survey in an indexed journal. Realistic model for a first-author survey.

examples_ortho.title: Evaluation of X-ray Personal protective equipment for Orthopaedic Surgeons in theatrE (EXPOSEd) study: a national survey of Trauma & Orthopaedic surgeons
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Trainee-led UK national survey with a memorable acronym and a workforce-safety angle.

typical_numbers.fact: Physician web surveys: 35% overall response (27-47% by specialty), with reminders adding substantially.
typical_numbers.source: Cunningham CT, Quan H, Hemmelgarn B, Noseworthy T, Beck CA, Dixon E, et al. Exploring physician specialist response rates to web-based surveys. BMC Med Res Methodol. 2015;15:32.

levels.appraisal_tool: JBI checklist for analytical cross-sectional studies; AXIS

levels.label: Case series
levels.short: Outcomes of a group treated the same way, no comparator.

potency.explanation: Describes what happened; cannot say whether the treatment caused it. Still useful for new techniques, rare conditions and complication rates.

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: High, but weak journals and lower ST3 value if the journal treats it as a short report.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: Often audit/service evaluation if describing local outcomes; research if generalisable claims.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts if published as a full original article in a PubMed + WoS journal. Does not count if it is really a case report or a technical tip. BJJ and many top journals rarely take them.

examples_ortho.title: Displaced proximal humeral fractures. I. Classification and evaluation
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Historic case series (about 300 patients) that produced the Neer classification. Case series can matter when they create a framework.

examples_ortho.title: The Oxford medial unicompartmental arthroplasty: a ten-year survival study
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Designer-surgeon implant survival series. Useful, but shows the limits: no comparator and designer bias.
examples_ortho.verification: PMID from the QxMD record + BJJ DOI page (PubMed page itself not fetched)

typical_numbers.fact: Level IV studies remained a large share of JBJS output over three decades even as Level I/II rose.
typical_numbers.source: Hanzlik S, Mahabir RC, Baynosa RC, Khiabani KT. Levels of evidence in research published in The Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery (American Volume) over the last thirty years. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2009.

levels.reporting_guideline: PROCESS (surgical case series) or STROBE elements
levels.appraisal_tool: JBI case series checklist; MINORS (non-comparative, max 16)

potency.explanation: Hypothesis-generating at best. Good for rare harms, teaching and learning to write.
raises: Genuinely new finding (first description of a harm)
lowers: Everything else: no comparator, no generalisability

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Very fast, but excluded for ST3 and rejected without review by BJJ.

counts_for_ST3.note: Excluded by name in the ST3 self-assessment. Do one only for learning or a teaching portfolio.

examples_ortho.title: A Squeaking Knee Is a Rare Complication of ACL Surgery: A Case Report
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Typical case report: one patient, one unusual complication. Fine for learning to write, excluded for ST3.

typical_numbers.fact: BJJ no longer accepts case reports and rejects them without review.
typical_numbers.source: BJJ instructions for authors (fetched 2026-10-21)

levels.label: Expert opinion, narrative review, mechanistic reasoning
levels.short: What experienced people think, or what biology predicts.
levels.grade_start: Not graded as evidence; GRADE treats opinion as interpretation, not data.

subtypes.name: Formal consensus (Delphi, nominal group)
subtypes.note: Structured and transparent (FRI consensus). Better than one person's view.

subtypes.name: Narrative / current concepts review
subtypes.note: Readable overview, no systematic search; open to cherry-picking.

subtypes.name: Mechanistic / lab / biomechanical
subtypes.note: Explains why, but cadaver and lab results often fail to predict clinical outcomes.

potency.explanation: Lowest certainty about effects. Formal consensus is highly cited and useful for definitions.
raises: Formal Delphi with pre-set agreement threshold
Linked to an SR of the evidence

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Narrative reviews are usually invited; consensus work needs senior leadership.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: None (Delphi of staff may need ethics review).

counts_for_ST3.note: A full review article in an indexed journal is a paper; editorials, letters and commentaries are excluded. Treat narrative reviews as low priority.

examples_ortho.title: Fracture-related infection: A consensus on definition from an international expert group
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Formal expert consensus. Very highly cited and useful, but it is still expert opinion, not trial evidence.

typical_numbers.fact: Delphi studies usually use 2-4 rounds and define consensus as 70-80% agreement in advance.
typical_numbers.source: Common Delphi methodology; check ACCORD reporting guideline.

side_categories.label: Diagnostic accuracy studies
side_categories.short: How well a test finds the condition against a reference standard.
side_categories.why_outside: Answers 'is the test accurate?', not 'does treatment work?'. Has its own ladder.
own_hierarchy: 1. SR of cross-sectional accuracy studies with a consistent reference standard and blinding (e.g. Cochrane DTA review)
2. Single cross-sectional study of consecutive patients, blinded, same reference standard for all
3. Non-consecutive patients, or reference standard not applied to all (partial verification)
4. Case-control (diagnostic) design: sick vs healthy people - inflates accuracy

potency.explanation: Strong when consecutive patients receive both tests with blinding. Spectrum bias and verification bias inflate sensitivity.
raises: Blinded index test and reference reading

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Good fit for on-call questions (scaphoid, occult hip, Ottawa rules).

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF.

examples_ortho.title: Computed tomography versus magnetic resonance imaging versus bone scintigraphy for clinically suspected scaphoid fractures in patients with negative plain radiographs
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Cochrane diagnostic test accuracy review with QUADAS-2 and bivariate models. The DTA gold standard in your field.

examples_ortho.title: Clinical usefulness of the Ottawa Ankle Rules in the overweight and obese population following an acute ankle injury: A prospective cross-sectional study
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Primary diagnostic accuracy study of a clinical rule in a defined subgroup. The sort of DTA question an on-call registrar can answer.

typical_numbers.fact: To estimate sensitivity of 90% with a 95% CI half-width of 5%, you need about 140 patients WITH the condition (Buderer approach).
typical_numbers.source: Standard sample size formula for sensitivity.

side_categories.label: Qualitative research
side_categories.short: Explores experiences, meanings and reasons, not numbers.
side_categories.why_outside: Answers 'why' and 'how' questions. Not ranked against RCTs; judged on rigour and fit for purpose.

potency.explanation: Judged by credibility, not by effect size. GRADE-CERQual rates confidence in qualitative review findings.
raises: Clear methodology (thematic analysis, IPA, grounded theory)
Purposive sampling to saturation or information power

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Good fit with your MSc Med Ed skills. Interviews are time-hungry.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: Patients: REC. Staff/trainees: HRA tool, often university ethics.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF.

examples_ortho.title: Patient and informal carer experience of hip fracture: a qualitative study using interviews and observation in acute orthopaedic trauma
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: UK qualitative study with interviews plus observation. Shows COREQ-style reporting in an indexed general journal.

examples_ortho.title: Patient experience of long-term recovery after open fracture of the lower limb: a qualitative study using interviews in a community setting
examples_ortho.journal: Journal not confirmed (likely BMJ Open; check)
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Qualitative interview study nested around a UK trauma trial population.

typical_numbers.fact: Interview studies commonly use 12-30 participants; justify with information power or saturation rather than a fixed number.
typical_numbers.source: Malterud 2016 information power concept; rule of thumb.

side_categories.label: Audit, quality improvement and service evaluation
side_categories.short: Measures local practice against a standard, or improves it.
side_categories.why_outside: Practice evaluation, not generalisable research. Tells you about Blackpool, not about the world.

potency.explanation: Low as evidence of effect elsewhere. A closed loop with run charts and a sustained change is more convincing.
raises: Two or more cycles with a real change in between

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Very high. You already have the distal radius audit and VTE service evaluation.

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full paper in a PubMed + WoS journal. BMJ Open Quality is PubMed-indexed; confirm its Web of Science status in the Master Journal List before relying on it. Audit also scores in its own ST3 domain.

examples_ortho.title: Quality improvement initiative: how the setting up of an anaesthesia consultant-led perioperative outreach service addressed anaesthesia-specific issues to improve anaesthesia consult and surgery timings for hip fracture patients
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Hip fracture QI paper in BMJ Open Quality using PDSA-style cycles and run charts.

examples_ortho.title: Reducing returns to theatre for neck of femur fracture patients
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Short UK QI report on hip fracture outcomes. Shows how small a publishable QI project can be.

typical_numbers.fact: Run charts need at least 10-12 baseline data points before you can call a shift or trend reliably.
typical_numbers.source: IHI run chart rules; rule of thumb.

side_categories.label: Educational research
side_categories.short: Does a teaching method change learning or performance?
side_categories.why_outside: Uses the same designs (RCT, cohort, survey, qualitative) but outcomes sit on Kirkpatrick levels, not patient outcomes.

potency.explanation: Rate it by the design used. Kirkpatrick level 3-4 (behaviour in theatre, patient outcomes) beats level 1 (satisfaction).
raises: Objective performance outcome (OSATS, simulator metrics, theatre performance)

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: High. Your MSc Med Ed and teaching role give you access and theory.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: HRA tool; often university ethics (Warwick) for trainees/students

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF. Medical Teacher, BMC Medical Education, J Surg Educ are PubMed + WoS.

examples_ortho.title: Transferring simulated arthroscopic skills to the operating theatre: a randomised blinded study
examples_ortho.why_it_is_a_good_example: Educational RCT in orthopaedics with blinded assessment of real theatre performance. Strong model for med-ed research.

typical_numbers.fact: Most surgical education RCTs randomise 20-60 trainees; power on an objective score, not on satisfaction.
typical_numbers.source: Rule of thumb.

side_categories.reporting_guideline: Use the design guideline (CONSORT, STROBE, COREQ); GREET for teaching interventions

side_categories.label: Scoping review
side_categories.short: Maps what exists and where the gaps are.
side_categories.why_outside: No pooling and usually no risk-of-bias appraisal, so it says what is known, not what works.

potency.explanation: Not evidence of effect. Valuable for setting agendas and core outcome sets.
lowers: Question so broad it maps everything

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: High. Good starter project for students and FY doctors.
effectiveness_for_him.approvals: None; register on OSF (PROSPERO does not take them)

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF.

examples_ortho.title: Artificial intelligence in orthopedic trauma surgery: a scoping review of current applications and research gaps

side_categories.label: Umbrella review (overview of reviews)

side_categories.why_outside: Sits above SRs in theory, but only as strong as the reviews it summarises and how overlap is handled.

potency.explanation: Useful when many conflicting MAs exist. Weakened by overlapping primary studies and low-quality included SRs.
raises: Re-analysis from primary data where needed
lowers: Counting the same trials many times

effectiveness_for_him.feasibility: Good in crowded fields (hip arthroscopy, TKA tech).

counts_for_ST3.note: Counts only as a full peer-reviewed paper in a journal indexed in BOTH PubMed and Web of Science, with you named personally (not only a group name). Re-check the current year's self-assessment PDF.

verification_note: Every PMID was matched to its exact title on pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov via PubMed-restricted search on 2026-10-21. Direct page fetches hit a CAPTCHA and Europe PMC rate-limited after two lookups, so only DRAFFT (two papers) has journal + year confirmed by API. Items with journal_year_confirmed=false need one glance on PubMed.
